what: A guard meant to stop a scratch file from ever being pushed judged the wrong thing and refused a file that was never going to be pushed at all. It asked whether a run's own declared-output list named a scratch-shaped file absent from the base commit — but a declared output that is git-ignored and never committed is *also* absent from the base commit, so a legitimate, ignored side-effect file was refused exactly like a real mistake would have been.
rule: A guard that exists to stop something from being pushed must judge the actual diff that would be pushed, never a list of what a job merely claims to have produced.
fix: Enforcement: the guard now reads the real diff between the base commit and the current one (plus anything staged) instead of the run's declared outputs. Regression coverage is in `tests/field-lessons-batch-m1.test.mjs`.
